name: Kisho Kurokawa
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded the Metabolist Movement and co-authored the Metabolism 1960 manifesto at the World Design Conference in Tokyo in 1960, at age 26.
early_history_summary: Kurokawa studied architecture at Kyoto University (BA 1957) and then at the University of Tokyo under Kenzo Tange (MA 1959), where he was exposed to experimental urban design concepts. The son of an architect, he was immersed in design from an early age and co-founded the Metabolist Movement at 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Kanie, Aichi Prefecture; son of architect Miki Kurokawa, immersed in the world of design from an early age. Also influenced by Buddhist teachings and traditional Japanese aesthetics.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an architect, providing early immersion in design thinking and architectural concepts.
primary_early_advantage_tags: architect father, Tange mentorship, Kyoto University, University of Tokyo, Metabolist colleagues, postwar reconstruction, WWII air raids
evidence_summary: Kurokawa was the son of architect Miki Kurokawa, giving him early exposure to design thinking. He trained at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo under Kenzo Tange, one of Japan's leading modernist architects, providing elite mentorship and network access. The postwar Japanese construction boom and reconstruction context created a structural wave. His experience of WWII air raids destroying his hometown shaped his architectural philosophy of impermanence and adaptability. By 26, he co-founded the Metabolist Movement with colleagues at the World Design Conference.
starting_point: Born in Kanie, Aichi Prefecture, Japan; son of architect Miki Kurokawa, immersed in design from an early age.
current_position: Died in October 2007 at age 73 in Tokyo; final role: founder and president of Kisho Kurokawa Architect & Associates, leading Japanese architect and Metabolist Movement co-founder.

trajectory.event: Graduated with a bachelor's degree in architecture from Kyoto University.
Completed master's degree at the University of Tokyo under architect Kenzo Tange.
Co-founded the Metabolist Movement and co-authored the Metabolism 1960 manifesto at the World Design Conference in Tokyo.
Established Kisho Kurokawa Architect & Associates in Tokyo.
Completed the Nakagin Capsule Tower in Tokyo, the landmark Metabolist project featuring detachable prefabricated capsules.
Received the Academie d'Architecture Gold Medal from France.
Completed the new exhibition wing at the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam.
Died of heart failure in Tokyo on October 12, 2007.

name: Svetlana Savitskaya
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Champion in aerobatics as a member of the Soviet national team at the FAI World Aerobatic Championships in Hullavington in July 1970 at age 22, and had already completed 450 parachute jumps and set multiple world records by her late teens.
early_history_summary: Savitskaya began parachuting secretly at age 16 without her parents' knowledge; her father, a WWII fighter ace and Deputy Commander of Soviet Air Defenses, supported her after discovering this. By 17 she had 450 jumps and record stratosphere dives. She enrolled at the Moscow Aviation Institute in 1966, became a licensed flight instructor in 1971, and joined the Soviet national aerobatics team from 1969 to 1977.
family_context_summary: Born into a privileged Soviet family; father Yevgeny Savitsky was a highly decorated WWII fighter pilot ace, twice Hero of the Soviet Union, and later Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Soviet Air Defense. Mother was a Muscovite Communist party leader.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a top-ranking military pilot who directly promoted and supported Svetlana's aviation career after discovering her secret parachuting training, providing access to military aviation networks and facilities.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father WWII ace, Soviet Air Defense deputy commander, MAI, Soviet national aerobatics team, parachuting records, military aviation network, Moscow
evidence_summary: Savitskaya was born into an exceptionally privileged aviation family; her father was a twice-Hero of the Soviet Union fighter ace who rose to Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Soviet Air Defenses. He directly supported her early aviation career after discovering her secret parachuting at 16. She had 450 parachute jumps by 17 and set stratosphere dive records. She enrolled at the elite Moscow Aviation Institute and became World Champion in aerobatics at 22. Her father's position provided access to military aviation networks, facilities, and the Soviet aviation pipeline.
starting_point: Born in Moscow to a privileged family; father was a decorated WWII fighter pilot ace and Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Soviet Air Defense, mother was a Communist party leader.
current_position: Retired cosmonaut and former member of the Russian State Duma representing CPRF; resides in Russia, second woman in space and first woman to perform a spacewalk.

trajectory.event: Completed 450 parachute jumps and set record stratosphere jumps from 14,250 m.

Flew aboard Soyuz T-7, becoming the second woman in space.
Became the first woman to fly to space twice and the first woman to perform a spacewalk on Soyuz T-12.
Elected to the Russian State Duma, later re-elected multiple times.

name: Ivo Daneu
milestone_by_age_26: Won the World Championship silver medal with Yugoslavia at the 1963 FIBA World Championship in Rio de Janeiro at age 26, having already won multiple Yugoslav League championships (1957, 1959, 1961, 1962) and debuted for the Yugoslav national team in 1957 at age 20.

He was noticed by Aleksandar Gec, who recommended him to the national coach, and he joined Olimpija Ljubljana at 19 in 1956. He made his European Championships debut in 1957 and quickly became a key national team player.
family_context_summary: Born in Maribor, Kingdom of Yugoslavia; his family was thrown out by the Germans during WWII, like many Slovenians. His first sport was tennis, then football, before switching to basketball.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early basketball start at 14, Branik Maribor, Olimpija Ljubljana, Aleksandar Gec mentorship, Yugoslav national team, wartime displacement
evidence_summary: Daneu started playing basketball at 14 for Branik Maribor and was recognized early for his rare talent by Aleksandar Gec, who recommended him to the national coach. He joined top Yugoslav club Olimpija Ljubljana at 19 and debuted for the Yugoslav national team at 20. His family was displaced during WWII, which may have contributed to his drive. He benefited from the rising Yugoslav basketball pipeline and sustained mentorship from Gec and national coach Aca Nikolic. By 26, he was a World Championship silver medalist and multiple-time Yugoslav League champion.
starting_point: Born in Maribor, Yugoslavia; family was displaced by the Germans during WWII; grew up in postwar Yugoslavia with modest circumstances.
current_position: Retired Slovenian basketball legend, FIBA Hall of Fame inductee (2007); resides in Slovenia, turned 88 in 2025.

Inducted into the FIBA Hall of Fame.

name: Ian Murdock
milestone_by_age_26: Founded the Debian GNU/Linux project in August 1993 at age 20 and wrote the Debian Manifesto in January 1994, creating one of the first and most influential Linux distributions with a decentralized open development model.
early_history_summary: Born in Konstanz, West Germany, where his father was pursuing postdoctoral research, Murdock grew up in Lafayette, Indiana after his father became a professor of entomology at Purdue University. He started programming at age 9 and studied at Purdue University. While a college student, he founded Debian in August 1993, inspired by dissatisfaction with existing Linux distributions and Linus Torvalds' sharing of Linux.
family_context_summary: Born in Konstanz, West Germany, where his father was pursuing postdoctoral research; family returned to the U.S. in 1975 and settled in Lafayette, Indiana in 1977 when his father became a professor of entomology at Purdue University. Middle-class academic family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an academic (entomology professor at Purdue); not in computer science but provided an academic environment and access to university resources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: programming from age 9, Purdue University, early Linux community, open source wave, academic family, internet distribution
evidence_summary: Murdock started programming at age 9 and grew up in an academic family with his father as a Purdue entomology professor, providing a middle-class environment with university access. He was immersed in the early Linux community at Purdue and founded Debian at 20, riding the open source wave of the early 1990s. His deep Unix/Linux knowledge was scarce for the era, and he leveraged internet distribution (FTP) from the start. No evidence of dedicated mentorship or exceptional peer cofounders was found; Debian was largely a self-created project driven by his technical depth and dissatisfaction with existing distributions.
starting_point: Born in Konstanz, West Germany to an academic family; father was pursuing postdoctoral research, later became a professor of entomology at Purdue University; grew up in Lafayette, Indiana from age 4.
current_position: Died on December 28, 2015 at age 42 in San Francisco; final role: Vice President of Platform and Developer Community at Salesforce Marketing Cloud, formerly founder of Debian and CTO of the Linux Foundation.

trajectory.event: Founded the Debian GNU/Linux project in August 1993 while a student at Purdue University, creating one of the first Linux distributions.
Wrote the Debian Manifesto in January 1994, establishing Debian's open development philosophy.
Graduated from Purdue with a BS in Computer Science and handed Debian leadership to Bruce Perens.
Co-founded Progeny Linux Systems, a commercial Linux company building custom Linux platforms.
Appointed CTO of the Free Standards Group and chair of the Linux Standard Base workgroup.
Joined Sun Microsystems as Vice President of Emerging Platforms to lead Project Indiana for OpenSolaris.
Died on December 28, 2015 in San Francisco; was working at Docker, Inc. at the time of his death.
